title: Baseball Cap Size Guide: One-Size, Fitted, Youth
h1: Baseball Cap Size Guide: How to Measure and Pick the Right Fit
description: Measure your head once and use this cap size chart to convert cm to fitted sizes 7 to 7 3/4, choose a one-size adjustable cap, and size youth caps.
tldr: An adjustable one-size cap fits head circumferences from 56 to 60 cm (7 to 7 1/2 on the fitted scale), which covers most adults.
Fitted caps run S to XL, from 7 (about 56 cm) to 7 3/4 (about 62 cm); measure in centimeters, then convert.
Measure around the widest part of your head, about 1 cm above the ears, with the tape snug but not tight.
Youth caps typically fit heads around 50 to 55 cm, with a shallower crown and a shorter brim than adult caps.
For a team or company order on one SKU, use an adjustable 56-60 cm cap; Raymark's custom MOQ is 50 pcs per colorway.
intro: Most cap fit problems start with a guess instead of a measurement. A soft tape around your head, read in centimeters, converts directly to one-size adjustable ranges and fitted hat sizes. This guide shows how to measure, how to read the chart, and what to do when you only get one SKU for a whole team.

sections.h2: What size baseball cap do you need?

blocks.text: You need the size that matches your head circumference in centimeters, and for most adults that lands between 56 and 60 cm, or roughly 7 to 7 1/2 on the fitted scale. An adjustable one-size cap covers that whole band with a strap or snapback at the rear, so one SKU serves a wide range of wearers.
A [fitted cap](/caps/pro-fit-fitted-cap/) is narrower: you buy one size, such as 7 1/4, with no take-up at the back. That is why fitted caps need a real measurement.

sections.h2: How do you measure head circumference at home?

blocks.text: Measure with a soft tape around the widest part of your head, about 1 cm above the ears. Keep the tape level and snug enough that it does not slide, but not tight enough to press into the skin.

items.title: Wrap the tape
items.text: Run a soft measuring tape around your head, crossing the forehead just above the eyebrows and the widest point at the back of the skull.

items.title: Check the level
items.text: The tape should sit level all the way around; a tape that dips at the back reads short and gives you a size that sits too low.

items.title: Read in centimeters
items.text: Note the number where the tape meets itself, rounded to the nearest half centimeter. Centimeters convert more cleanly than inches to cap sizes.

items.title: Measure twice
items.text: Take a second reading after resetting the tape. If the two numbers differ by more than 1 cm, take a third and use the middle value.

blocks.title: Hair and hats
blocks.text: Measure with your hair in the state you normally wear it under a cap. A thick bun or a pinned-up braid can add 1-2 cm to the reading and push you into the next size.

sections.h2: What do fitted sizes S to XL and 7 to 7 3/4 mean?

blocks.text: Fitted sizes come from the traditional hat scale, where the number is your head circumference in inches, divided into eighths. A 7 1/4 cap is made for a head about 22 3/4 inches, or 58 cm.
Letter bands overlap between makers, and a size that runs true in one crown height can feel tight in another. When ordering fitted styles for a group, ask for the centimeter range behind each letter.

sections.h2: How do crown height and brim width change the fit?

blocks.text: Crown height changes how deep the cap sits, and brim width changes how much shade and visual weight the cap carries. Neither is captured by the head measurement, which is why two caps in the same size can feel different.

A mid crown of roughly 10-12 cm suits most wearers, a high crown of 12-13 cm leaves room above the head, and a low crown of 8-9 cm suits smaller heads and worn-low styling. Brims commonly run 6.5-7.5 cm deep, and a wide, flat brim changes how the cap balances on the face even though the headband fit is unchanged.
Youth caps are not simply smaller adult caps. They are usually built for heads around 50-55 cm, with a shallower crown and shorter brim so the cap does not drop over a child's eyes.

Some youth caps are adjustable within that band; others are fitted in S/M. If a child measures 54-55 cm, an adjustable adult cap on its smallest setting can work, though the crown will look deep. Measure before ordering, and re-measure each season.

sections.h2: What if you are between sizes, and why does an adjustable strap hide it?

blocks.text: Between sizes, take the larger option when you plan to wear the cap low or have thick hair, and the smaller one when you want a snug, high fit. On an adjustable cap the strap covers the gap: a 57 cm head and a 60 cm head can both wear the same cap because the strap takes up the slack.

That convenience hides two things. Crown depth and brim shape do not change with the strap, so the same cap can feel right on one wearer and too deep on another. A strap pulled to its last hole also leaves a gap and a puckered rear panel.

blocks.title: Five-minute fit test
blocks.text: Wear the cap for five minutes before you commit. A red line on your forehead within that time means the band is too small, whatever the label says.

sections.h2: How do you size a team or company order when you only get one SKU?

blocks.text: For a one-SKU order, choose an adjustable cap built for 56-60 cm and accept that a few outliers will need a different size. Collect head measurements from the people who will actually wear the caps, then count how many fall inside the band.

items: Ask for centimeters, not S/M/L, because letters vary by maker
Count wearers inside 56-60 cm; if more than about one in five falls outside, price a second size
Order caps with the strap set loose so wearers can fine-tune on delivery

blocks.title: Mind the minimum
blocks.text: Raymark's MOQ is 50 pcs per style/colorway, so a size split inside one colorway is easier than adding a second colorway. Confirm the split in your quote request.

faqs.q: Is a one-size cap really one size?
faqs.a: It is one SKU with an adjustable band, built to cover about 56-60 cm. It fits most adults, but not every adult, and fit still depends on crown depth and brim shape.

faqs.q: What size cap fits a 58 cm head?
faqs.a: A 58 cm head is a 7 1/4 fitted cap, usually labeled M/L. Any adjustable one-size cap in the 56-60 cm range will also fit.

faqs.q: Do fitted caps stretch over time?
faqs.a: A leather sweatband may soften and break in slightly, but the cap itself does not stretch a full size. Buy the size that fits on day one.

faqs.q: Can I shrink a cap that is too big?
faqs.a: There is no reliable way to shrink a cotton cap without distorting the crown and brim. If the cap is too big, an adjustable style or a smaller fitted size is the practical fix.

faqs.q: How do I measure a child's head for a cap?
faqs.a: Use the same method as an adult: a soft tape around the widest point, about 1 cm above the ears. Most children fall near 50-55 cm, but measure rather than guessing by age.
